excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content:
Good that more and more people understands fuzz testing. I want to comment and answer some questions related to my work: libfuzzer based EOF validation.

libfuzzer provides coverage-guided (not only) fuzzing. It test an input on given code and collects a coverage "path" of execution. if the "path" is unique the new test is added to "corpus".

I initialized the corpus with evmone's unit tests.

There are 2 additional features in libfuzzer:
1. it can reduce tests: shorter test with the same coverage path replaces the longer one.
2. it can merge multiple dirs of tests: only tests which increase coverage are added.

Considering we have tests in ethereum/tests, EEST and evmone, we can use the fuzzer as the quality tool. Exporting EOF bytecodes from EEST will be handy. The fuzzer expects a file with raw bytecode (no hex) and you can name it as you want, e.g. "eest-test-name".

This way we can check if there are any unique test cases in any of EEST, ethereum/tests, evmone and the fuzzer itself.
